report:
### Conclusion
Yes, denosumab (Prolia) significantly reduces the risk of vertebral fractures in patients with osteoporosis. 

### Evidence Summary
The primary evidence supporting denosumab's effectiveness comes from pivotal clinical research, most notably the landmark 3-year FREEDOM trial:

* **Fracture Reduction Efficacy:** In postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, subcutaneous injections of denosumab (60 mg every 6 months for 36 months) significantly reduced the incidence of new vertebral fractures compared to placebo, as well as reducing hip and nonvertebral fractures.
* **Broad Efficacy Across Patient Subgroups:** Denosumab effectively reduces new morphometric vertebral fracture risk regardless of baseline age, initial bone mineral density (BMD), baseline rate of bone turnover, or prior fracture history.
* **Long-Term Efficacy:** Results from the 10-year FREEDOM Extension study demonstrated that extended denosumab treatment produces progressive, incremental gains in BMD while sustaining low rates of vertebral fractures over long-term follow-up.

Overall, clinical consensus and landmark trial data establish denosumab as a highly effective anti-osteoporosis therapy for fracture prevention.

### Sources
* New England Journal of Medicine: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa0809493
* The American Journal of Managed Care: https://www.ajmc.com/view/study-summary-freedom
* American Academy of Family Physicians: https://www.aafp.org/afp/2019/0501/od1
* PubMed Central (PMC): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8799550/
